decisions_taken_during_the_phase.mid-body && lists are NOT a set -e hazar: CANCELLED a 143-site sweep. Owner verified on 5.2.37 and 5.3.9, and it was re-verified here: bash exits only for the command following the FINAL && or ||, so a failing LEFT operand — the debug-log idiom `[[ "${VERBOSE_KKLASS:-}" == "debug" ]] && echo ... >&2` that sits on every error path — does not abort; the documented `return 1` is reached. Live proof on a real unit: `set -e; TList.new L; L.Get 5 || echo reached` prints 'reached' on both bashes. Only TWO shapes actually abort, and the plan named both from the start: (a) a TRAILING list as the last statement of a function, (b) a bare command whose non-zero status IS its answer.
decisions_taken_during_the_phase.trailing lists: none to fix: A scan of all 17 units for 'last statement of a function is an && list' found 3 hits, all intentional rc-predicates (dateutils._two/_three, thashset TSet._isSet), and EVERY call site already guards them with `|| return 1` or `if !`. Zero code changes needed.
decisions_taken_during_the_phase.bare status-as-value commands: 3 real bu: Found by the new contract tests, not by code reading: TArray._cmp3 and the sort merge loop called a user comparator bare (its rc 0/1/2 IS the answer), TStringList._sortcmp did the same, and TRegEx._match1 ran a bare `[[ =~ ]]` whose rc is the match answer. All three now capture the status with `|| rc=$?`.
decisions_taken_during_the_phase.bare arithmetic: `(( ... )) || :`: `(( x++ ))` returns 1 when x was 0 and `(( n -= 1 ))` returns 1 when the result is 0 — the plan's `+= 1` fixes only the increment half. One idiom for all 30 bare arithmetic statements, documented in kcl/README.md section 1.4.
decisions_taken_during_the_phase.kk.debug helper: Deduplicating the 66 identical debug-log lines behind a `kk.debug` helper is worth doing but is cosmetic; deferred to P9 on the owner's call (two mechanical sweeps had already misfired in this phase).
